subject: Latency runbook sync & load-test window coordination
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@acme.com>
Cc: ops@acme.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Latency runbook sync & load-test window coordination

Hi team,

We need to lock in a 60–90 minute deep-dive this week to align on the performance runbook and the load-test windows with Acme. Goals here: validate the runbook steps, confirm target token throughput and latency SLOs, and agree on the host/network access required for the Acme SREs.

High-level targets we want to validate during the session (proposed):
- Sustained token throughput: 120k tokens/sec across the cluster; allow 200k token/sec 60s spike for burst testing.
- Latency targets (inference path, 1024 seq): p50 < 60ms, p95 < 150ms, p99 < 400ms.
- Failure modes to exercise: node preemption, small-batch fallbacks, cache warmups.

Environment notes: runbook draft assumes dedicated capacity in us-west-2 (4x A100-80GB equivalent; model: redwood-1.3b-quant), prefix/KV cache enabled, and kernel selection pinned to mixed-FP16/INT8 path for stable tail latency. See attached runbook draft and the test matrix for initial batch-size / concurrency permutations.

Proposed windows (all PST):
- Mon 11/22 09:00–10:30
- Tue 11/23 13:00–14:30
- Wed 11/24 08:00–09:30

Please reply with preferred windows and any absolute constraints. Also: Marcus, can you confirm whether the dedicated pool can be reserved for the entire 2-hour block (including setup) and whether we can enable expanded trace logging during the run?

Maria/Acme: we will need an IP allowlist and a short-term service account for ingestion of the synthetic load. I added ops@acme.com on the cc to start procurement of permit details.

Attachments: latency_runbook_v0.3.md (draft), loadtest_matrix_20261120.csv (test permutations)

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
+dylan.brooks@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:36:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Latency runbook sync & load-test window coordination

Thanks Dylan — quick technical notes before we lock a slot.

On Fri, Nov 20, 2026 at 09:02 AM Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com> wrote:
> We need to lock in a 60–90 minute deep-dive this week to align on the performance runbook and the load-test windows with Acme.

Couple of asks from infra:
- For the 120k sustained target we should aim for 6x 20k token/sec workers (concurrency 8–12 each) rather than a single large fanout; that keeps KV cache locality and avoids head-of-line stalls. Please confirm if Acme's client can emit parallel streams.
- Kernel selection: the mixed-FP16/INT8 path is good but for p99 latency testing we want a fallback run on pure FP16 to rule out quantization tail artifacts. Add that as a second phase in the matrix.
- We can reserve the dedicated pool but need a 2hr block to include warmup and log collection (so reserve 09:00–11:00 if you pick the morning window).

I can do Tue 11/23 13:00–14:30 (preferred) or Wed morning. I’ll attach a short checklist for enabling expanded tracing — low-risk but adds ~5% overhead.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@acme.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@acme.com, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 10:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Latency runbook sync & load-test window coordination

Thanks — Acme SRE here. Tue 11/23 13:00–14:30 PST works for our team. A few operational items: 

- IP allowlist: we can open the subnet for the dedicated hosts, but we need the egress IPs you’ll be using. Can you provide those?
- Service account: ops@acme.com will create a short-lived service account with a key we can rotate post-test. Please send the exact scopes required.
- Data sensitivity: we will only run synthetic payloads — please confirm no real customer data paths will be hit and that logs are scrubbed for PII.

Doc links: procurement has asked for a short statement of work (SOW) for the reserved window — I’ve uploaded a template here: https://acme.share/sow-template. We’ll use that to approve the reserved capacity charge.

If Marcus wants to run an FP16 fallback phase, we’ll need an extra 30 minutes — can you bake that into the 2hr reservation?

—Maria
Maria Gonzalez
Senior SRE, Acme Corp

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@acme.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@acme.com
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 15:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Latency runbook sync & load-test window coordination

Perfect — locking Tue 11/23 12:45–14:45 PST (includes 15 minute setup and extra 30 minute FP16 fallback) and I’ll send a calendar invite with the Zoom link and our test run checklist.

Action items assigned:
- Dylan: reserve dedicated pool 12:30–15:00 (warmup + traces). Send egress IPs and required scopes by EOD Mon.
- Marcus: finalize tracing checklist and add FP16 fallback phase to test_matrix_20261120.csv.
- Karthik: confirm client-side parallel streams support & send a small sample generator for our infra team.
- Laura: prepare SOW outline for procurement and share with Maria’s ops contact.
- Maria/Acme: share permit details & SOW approval timeline.

Attachments referenced: latency_runbook_v0.3.md, loadtest_matrix_20261120.csv

Thanks everyone — see you Tue.

Dylan Brooks
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
